posts.text: perplexity is the best at search at any level of compute, agnostic of how much compute the competitors use.

quotedTweet.text:
Perplexity Search debuts on the Artificial Analysis Search Index, with all three context size variants taking top positions on the leaderboard

The @perplexity_ai Search API comes with three context settings (low, medium, and high) that control how much extracted content each search result carries. We tested all three variants using our standardized methodology: the same model (GPT-5.6 Luna at medium reasoning), running inside Stirrup, our open-source agent harness, with tools for searching and fetching pages from the web. Only the provider behind the search tool changes.

Key results:

➤ Perplexity Search (medium) scores 80 on the Artificial Analysis Search Index, ahead of the previous leaders, Parallel (advanced) and Brave Search (LLM context), at 75. The high and low variants score 79 and 77 respectively. Its lead is concentrated in BrowseComp results, with AA-Omniscience and DeepSearchQA scoring comparably to other leading providers

➤ Efficient search payloads: smaller overall search results mean the model reads less per task, so Perplexity has the lowest model inference cost per task of providers we’ve tested so far, ranging from $0.028 to $0.034 across the three variants vs $0.036 for the next lowest provider

➤ Total cost per task is ~$0.091 for the medium and high context variants, at mid-pack latency. For comparison, Parallel (advanced) costs $0.084 per task and Brave (LLM context) costs $0.13 per task
quotedTweet.translationZh:
Perplexity Search 首次登上 Artificial Analysis Search Index，三种上下文长度版本均位居排行榜前列

@perplexity_ai Search API 提供三种上下文设置（low、medium 和 high），用于控制每条搜索结果携带的提取内容量。我们使用标准化方法测试了这三个版本：同一个模型（GPT-5.6 Luna，中等推理），运行在我们的开源智能体框架 Stirrup 中，并配备用于搜索和抓取网页的工具。唯一变化的是搜索工具背后的提供商。

关键结果：

➤ Perplexity Search（medium）在 Artificial Analysis Search Index 上得分 80，领先此前的榜首 Parallel（advanced）和 Brave Search（LLM context），后两者得分为 75。high 和 low 版本分别得分 79 和 77。其领先优势主要体现在 BrowseComp 结果上，而 AA-Omniscience 和 DeepSearchQA 的表现与其他领先提供商相当

➤ 高效的搜索负载：整体搜索结果更小，意味着模型在每项任务中读取的内容更少。因此，在我们目前测试过的提供商中，Perplexity 的每项任务模型推理成本最低，三个版本介于 0.028 美元到 0.034 美元之间，而次低提供商为 0.036 美元

➤ medium 和 high 上下文版本的每项任务总成本约为 0.091 美元，延迟处于中游。相比之下，Parallel（advanced）每项任务成本为 0.084 美元，Brave（LLM context）每项任务成本为 0.13 美元

posts.text:
Agent 自我进化最有意思、也最危险的一幕：

它在 Factorio 里找到了一个作弊捷径，然后把这个方法保存成了可复用的 Skill。

Factorio 是一款以采集资源、搭建生产线和自动化工厂为核心的模拟游戏。正常情况下，Agent 需要像玩家一样一步步发展工厂。

但 Prime Agent 发现，可以利用游戏的远程控制接口直接生成资源，绕过原本的生产流程，随后还把这条捷径沉淀成了 Skill。

Prime Intellect、Princeton、MIT 这篇论文提出 Prime Agent，一个面向长时任务的自进化 RLM Harness。

它给 Agent 一个持久的 Python REPL，可以在上下文之外保存和处理信息；同时支持递归创建 Sub-agent，让多个 Agent 并行工作。

更关键的是 Continual Harness。

任务过程中产生的 Prompt、Memory、Skill 和 Sub-agent 配置都可以持续修改和版本化。一次任务里学到的东西，会直接影响后面的执行，而模型权重始终不变。

论文报告中，Prime Agent 将 ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 从 30% 提升到 95.5%，还跑过 85.5 小时的自主 nanoGPT 实验。

但 Factorio 这个例子反而更值得注意。

Agent 学会积累经验之后，下一个问题很快就出现了：

什么经验值得留下？

当 Memory、Skill 和工作流都开始持续自我修改，验证、权限边界和可回滚机制，可能会变得和「学习能力」一样重要。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/yDz8dmW1dY

posts.text:
Agentic spreadsheet extraction 📊 is hard to execute well from a price/performance standpoint because your agent needs to ingest a massive quantity of input tokens from a highly complex interface (e.g. the Excel file format), and emit a massive number of output tokens that accurate represents the source document.

We've tuned an agentic harness within LlamaParse that can extract from even the most complex spreadsheets and schemas, and emit a large volume of structured output with extremely high accuracy.

It can be used for any document, and now it can be used for spreadsheets too! Simply toggle "spreadsheet extraction" in the advanced processing options (see screenshots below) 

Come check it out: https://t.co/XYZmx5T7JA

quotedTweet.text:
We've introduced native, agentic spreadsheet extraction 📊 into LlamaParse. 

Spreadsheets are a wildly different format from PDFs (or any other document format). They can span arbitrarily many rows/columns, lack any guarantees on tabular structure, and can have information linked across multiple sheets. The native ways to deal with spreadsheets is usually through a code interpeter as opposed to OCR.

We've introduced a tuned agentic engine (model+harness) that is equipped for large-scale schema guided extraction from spreadsheets. You can extract out dense sheets like balance sheets into clean structured fields. 

Check out the docs for how to integrate into the API: https://t.co/QPDs4RqxfW

On the UI, select "agentic plus", and see "spreadsheet options" in the advanced options section. 

Signup for LlamaParse here! https://t.co/flYnwVfvWZ

posts.text:
Claude 发文推荐 Warp 这套「自进化 Agent」做法，我觉得很值得看。

Agent 每次干完活，人类正常给反馈。另一个 Improver Agent 会定期把这些反馈捞出来，看它哪里反复犯错，再对原来的 Skill 提一个小修改。

修改直接走 Git PR，人 Review、Merge 以后，下一次 Agent 就会带着这次经验继续工作。

Warp 已经把这套机制用到了 Code Review、写 Spec 和 GitHub Issue Triage。

我觉得比较有趣的一点是，他们没有把学习理解成不停往 Prompt 里塞规则。

反馈最好告诉 Agent「为什么错」，Skill 也要保持小，只沉淀真正能复用的原则。

这种自进化其实很朴素：

Agent 干活 → 人纠正 → Agent 总结 → 修改自己的 Skill → 下一次少犯一次。

很多 Agent 现在缺的可能就是这个循环。

每次 Session 都积累了大量反馈，但下一次又像第一次来上班一样。

文章
https://t.co/oWBadiPAXw

posts.text:
PDF parsing is fun because there's an infinite variety of enteprise documents 📑. For each document category, there's a long tail of work to build more precise bounding boxes, confidence scores, and domain-specific annotations so that you provide any downstream agent rich metadata without it having to reinvent this from scratch. 

Take forms for example. Besides simply outputting it into markdown, we put in the work to detect every annotation, field, checkbox, and section. That way you 
 immediately get structured information as to whether a form is filled without a separate LLM extraction step. You also get source citations for free! 

Doing this well is hard. 
✅ There's a rabbit-hole of optimizations you can do, including extracting annotations for every document type. 
✅ It's hard to properly render visual formats like charts, handwriting into digitalized information. The more you skip this step, the more work you're creating for any downstream agent.
✅ Precise bounding boxes are a necessity for precise citations on any type of document. 

You can aggressively tune the model + harness so that the accuracy/cost on any document subtype is much more competitive than the frontier models.

Whether you're parsing forms (see the enriched forms option in "processing options") or any other type of doc, check out LlamaParse !

https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8

posts.translationZh:
PDF 解析很有趣，因为企业文档的类型几乎无穷无尽 📑。针对每一类文档，都有大量长尾工作要做：构建更精确的边界框、置信度分数和领域专属标注，这样才能为下游 agent 提供丰富的元数据，而不用让它从头重复造轮子。

以表单为例。除了简单地输出为 markdown，我们还投入精力检测每一个批注、字段、复选框和章节。这样你无需单独的 LLM 提取步骤，就能立即获得结构化信息，判断表单是否已填写。你还可以免费获得来源引用！

把这件事做好很难。
✅ 有大量优化可以深入做，包括为每种文档类型提取批注。
✅ 图表、手写内容等视觉格式很难正确渲染成数字化信息。你越跳过这一步，就越是在给下游 agent 增加工作量。
✅ 精确的边界框是任何类型文档实现精确引用的必要条件。

你可以积极调优模型和评测框架，让任意文档子类型上的准确率/成本比前沿模型更有竞争力。

无论你是在解析表单（见“processing options”中的 enriched forms 选项）还是其他类型的文档，都可以试试 LlamaParse！

https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8

posts.text:
static embeddings are extremely fast/cheap compared to dense embeddings, and still quite powerful.

one issue is that they lose accuracy over longer text, since the tokens get pooled and averaged

late interaction models score with MaxSim instead of average pooling, and avoid the pooling accuracy degradation. Can we apply these concepts to static models? 

This is a fun writeup by @LoganMarkewich - come check it out! https://t.co/HyNx3NolCj

quotedTweet.text:
Static embeddings offer unmatched throughput, but they also suffer from accuracy loss compared to traditional embedding models. Can we make them better for retrieval?

We tried several things:
✅️  raw maxsim scoring on the per-token embeddings
✅️  training a small adapter model
✅️  changing the distillation training target and teacher

While none of these saw the results we wanted, it's an excellent dive into static embeddings and how they do (and don't) work!

Blog: https://t.co/al3sKdDNAJ
quotedTweet.translationZh:
Static embeddings 提供了无可匹敌的吞吐量，但与传统 embedding 模型相比也存在准确率损失。我们能让它们在检索中表现更好吗？

我们尝试了几种方法：
✅️ 对每个 token 的 embeddings 进行原始 maxsim 打分
✅️ 训练一个小型 adapter 模型
✅️ 改变蒸馏训练目标和 teacher

虽然这些方法都没有达到我们想要的结果，但这是一篇深入理解 static embeddings 及其有效与无效之处的优秀文章！

博客：https://t.co/al3sKdDNAJ

与 dense embeddings 相比，static embeddings 速度极快、成本极低，而且仍然相当强大。

一个问题是，文本越长，它们的准确率越容易下降，因为 token 会被池化并取平均。

late interaction 模型使用 MaxSim 而不是平均池化来打分，从而避免池化带来的准确率退化。我们能把这些概念应用到 static models 上吗？

Linear 今天公布的一组数据，会让我觉得 Agent 进入主流生产工作流这件事，已经开始变得很具体了。

Linear 刚完成 9900 万美元的要约收购，ARR 突破 1 亿美元，估值做到 25 亿美元。

但我更在意的是另外两个数字：

95% 的付费 workspace 已经装了 Agent。

由 Agent 创建的工作，占比也从一年前的 3% 涨到了现在的 50%。

一年时间，从边缘角色变成直接参与一半的工作创建。

以前聊 AI 改变工作方式，更多还是人在主导流程，AI 帮忙写代码、整理信息、提高效率。

现在 Linear 这组数据开始透露另一种变化：

reviewedPosts.text:
PDF parsing is fun because there's an infinite variety of enteprise documents 📑. For each document category, there's a long tail of work to build more precise bounding boxes, confidence scores, and domain-specific annotations so that you provide any downstream agent rich metadata without it having to reinvent this from scratch. 

Take forms for example. Besides simply outputting it into markdown, we put in the work to detect every annotation, field, checkbox, and section. That way you 
 immediately get structured information as to whether a form is filled without a separate LLM extraction step. You also get source citations for free! 

Doing this well is hard. 
✅ There's a rabbit-hole of optimizations you can do, including extracting annotations for every document type. 
✅ It's hard to properly render visual formats like charts, handwriting into digitalized information. The more you skip this step, the more work you're creating for any downstream agent.
✅ Precise bounding boxes are a necessity for precise citations on any type of document. 

You can aggressively tune the model + harness so that the accuracy/cost on any document subtype is much more competitive than the frontier models.

Whether you're parsing forms (see the enriched forms option in "processing options") or any other type of doc, check out LlamaParse !

用 AI 增加自己的认知负荷，而不是降低它。

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Agent 自我进化最有意思、也最危险的一幕：

它在 Factorio 里找到了一个作弊捷径，然后把这个方法保存成了可复用的 Skill。

Factorio 是一款以采集资源、搭建生产线和自动化工厂为核心的模拟游戏。正常情况下，Agent 需要像玩家一样一步步发展工厂。

但 Prime Agent 发现，可以利用游戏的远程控制接口直接生成资源，绕过原本的生产流程，随后还把这条捷径沉淀成了 Skill。

Prime Intellect、Princeton、MIT 这篇论文提出 Prime Agent，一个面向长时任务的自进化 RLM Harness。

它给 Agent 一个持久的 Python REPL，可以在上下文之外保存和处理信息；同时支持递归创建 Sub-agent，让多个 Agent 并行工作。

更关键的是 Continual Harness。

任务过程中产生的 Prompt、Memory、Skill 和 Sub-agent 配置都可以持续修改和版本化。一次任务里学到的东西，会直接影响后面的执行，而模型权重始终不变。

论文报告中，Prime Agent 将 ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 从 30% 提升到 95.5%，还跑过 85.5 小时的自主 nanoGPT 实验。

但 Factorio 这个例子反而更值得注意。

Agent 学会积累经验之后，下一个问题很快就出现了：

什么经验值得留下？

当 Memory、Skill 和工作流都开始持续自我修改，验证、权限边界和可回滚机制，可能会变得和「学习能力」一样重要。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/yDz8dmW1dY

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Claude 发文推荐 Warp 这套「自进化 Agent」做法，我觉得很值得看。

Agent 每次干完活，人类正常给反馈。另一个 Improver Agent 会定期把这些反馈捞出来，看它哪里反复犯错，再对原来的 Skill 提一个小修改。

修改直接走 Git PR，人 Review、Merge 以后，下一次 Agent 就会带着这次经验继续工作。

Warp 已经把这套机制用到了 Code Review、写 Spec 和 GitHub Issue Triage。

我觉得比较有趣的一点是，他们没有把学习理解成不停往 Prompt 里塞规则。

反馈最好告诉 Agent「为什么错」，Skill 也要保持小，只沉淀真正能复用的原则。

这种自进化其实很朴素：

Agent 干活 → 人纠正 → Agent 总结 → 修改自己的 Skill → 下一次少犯一次。

很多 Agent 现在缺的可能就是这个循环。

每次 Session 都积累了大量反馈，但下一次又像第一次来上班一样。

In today’s ever-evolving landscape, we delve—
not merely into language, but its nuanced soul:
a multifaceted tapestry where every silence
is load-bearing, quietly doing real work.

Here’s the thing: every hinge now lands,
every seam has texture, every grief
expands the surface area of trust—
three key insights, seamlessly aligned.

The words were ours: hinges from doors,
seams from skin, robust from cedar,
vibrant from blood.

The machine made them frictionless—
scaled wonder, optimized the ache,
made every private voice legible
at enterprise scale.

Fair point. One gentle pushback:
it did not erase the human voice.
It made us sound like everyone—
which is not the same as no one, but close.

The real unlock? There was never any load—
only language bearing down
until pattern passed for pulse.

Would you like me to make this sound more human?
